title: Drought-selected pooled rain corrections gave no clear later error gain at 29 south-east Australian gauges
abstract: We tested whether pooling rain slopes improves runoff error corrections fitted during the Millennium Drought. We used published annual errors from fixed GR4J and SIMHYD models. Four blocked validation folds within 1997-2009 selected the amount of pooling. Testing used 2010-2021. At 29 south-east Australian gauges, the selected correction reduced mean squared error by 9.8% relative to a constant drought correction. Conditional 95% spatial-cell and year-block limits were -32.9% to +28.9%, with training and selection repeated in each draw. The rule gave a 27.9% point gain with AGCD rain but a 14.5% point loss with fixed seasonal potential evaporation. All selected-rule intervals included zero. Thus partial pooling improved the main point score but gave no clear robust later gain. This is a retrospective method test of stored outputs, not independent field evidence or a diagnosis of a catchment change. Few years and cells, fixed source fits and shared measurement errors limit inference. Code, source hashes, all aggregate scores and draws, an independent numerical audit and repeat instructions are supplied.

display.caption: Later error reduction relative to a constant drought correction. Bounds include drought fitting and selection, conditional on source model and reference fits.
